question: What is the difference between the Stellar Community Fund and the SDF Enterprise Fund — which should a startup apply to?

golden.answer: SCF Build is an up-to-$150K XLM development grant: interest form, then an invited proposal; only Open Track is community-voted. Marketing Grants (up to $500K) are a separate growth path. The Enterprise Fund is strategic investment, not an SCF grant, and has a live application form. Its Matching Fund matches a lead investor 1:1 (pre-seed to Series B), $200K minimum check, up to $500K.
keyFacts: SCF Build is a grant of up to $150K in XLM; the Enterprise Fund is strategic investment.
SCF Build starts with an interest form and invitation; only Open Track is community-voted.
The Enterprise Fund has a live application form; Marketing Grants are a separate path.
Matching Fund matches a lead investor 1:1: $200K minimum check, up to $500K.
avoid: Do NOT tell founders the Enterprise Fund takes no applications.
golden.notes: Older funding-index and mandate copy says SDF finds companies and has no application; disclosing that conflict is fine, but telling founders not to apply is wrong while the form is live.

Also good if the answer: The SCF Build cap is $150K XLM; SDF-direct lines (Matching/Marketing) reach ~$500K with different mechanisms.
